Fwding FinTechX's ask. They need options and a quick MAP to get procurement unstuck. Draft notes below — please review and add technical or legal constraints before I send.

Draft proposal (high level):
- Base configuration recommendations:
  * Option A (throughput-optimized): 8x H100-80GB in a single pool (preferred for peak throughput and perf/$ on large-batch workloads). Handles bursts to ~320 qps with aggressive batching and autoscale.
  * Option B (balanced): 12x A100-80GB (better NVMe/local memory economics for steady qps; slightly lower peaktoken throughput for large batches but good for KV-heavy flows).
  * Option C (cost-optimized): 16x L40S-48GB (lower unit cost; good for short-token, high-concurrency inference; less headroom for huge KV caches).
- Memory considerations: H100 gives best perf for large KV cache + longer contexts; A100 is solid for steady-state and quantization; L40S best when per-GPU mem needs are moderate and you want density.
- Pricing / commit tiers (internal draft):
  * 12mo commit: 15% list discount on hosted dedicated pool rate
  * 24mo commit: 22% list discount + 2% credit back if we meet 99.95% uptime SLA
  * 36mo commit: 28% list discount + 5% onboarding credit (one-time)
- Throughput guarantees: offer SLO language with credits (pro-rated pool-month credits) for sustained missed P50/P95 latencies; legal will need to sign off.

Open asks for Marcus: do you have perf/$ numbers for short prompt qps vs batch throughput across H100/A100/L40S (ballpark) and any cautions on KV cache sizes per GPU? Also: recommended autoscale headroom and burst policy.

I’ll tailor the final message to Anna with the three options, attached pricing sheet, and a proposed MAP if you OK.

Karthik / Laura,

Quick technical notes and ballpark perf/$ estimates (based on our internal benchmarks — see attached CSV for test details):

- Short prompts (<= 64 tokens) w/ high QPS (stateless inference):
  * L40S-48GB: best $/qps at small context; expect ~1.8x perf/$ vs A100 for tiny-token workloads due to density and lower cost.
  * A100-80GB: baseline; good latency and decent batching.
  * H100-80GB: higher raw throughput but higher list price; perf/$ roughly parity or slightly better than A100 at large batch sizes.

- Long-context / KV cache heavy (contexts > 8k tokens):
  * H100-80GB recommended — larger HBM and Tensor core improvements matter for attention ops and KV cache hit persistence. For large KV caches per request, you'll want fewer larger GPUs to avoid cross-GPU sharding overhead.
  * A100-80GB OK if they plan to quantize aggressively and keep model variants small; watch memory fragmentation.

- Perf/$ example (very rough):
  * L40S: baseline cost unit = 1.0; effective qps/unit = 1.0 -> perf/$ = 1.0
  * A100: cost unit = 2.2; effective qps/unit = 1.6 -> perf/$ ≈ 0.73
  * H100: cost unit = 3.8; effective qps/unit = 3.0 -> perf/$ ≈ 0.79
  => L40S wins cost-effectively for short prompts. H100 wins for large-batch or long-context where throughput scales better.

- KV cache sizing per GPU (guidance):
  * H100-80GB: comfortably support ~35–45 GB of usable KV per GPU after overheads.
  * A100-80GB: ~30–40 GB usable.
  * L40S-48GB: ~20–28 GB usable — could force more cross-GPU sync for large contexts.

- Autoscale & buffer guidance: target pool that covers steady-state (80 qps) + 20% headroom; burst policy using ephemeral preemptible nodes for spike capacity if they want cheaper burst. For strict SLOs, prefer fewer larger GPUs (H100s) to reduce inter-GPU comms.

I attached gpu_benchmark_appendix.csv with the run configs. Legal / pricing: Marcus, these perf numbers support a smaller L40S-first proposal for cost-conscious procurement, but we should show H100 option for SLA-sensitive workloads.

—Marcus
Senior Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear requirements. Below are three concrete options tailored to the 80 qps steady / 300 qps burst profile you described, plus pricing and next steps. Attached: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf, sla_terms_dedicated.docx, gpu_benchmark_appendix.csv

1) Throughput-first (recommended if bursts drive value)
  - Pool: 8x H100-80GB dedicated
  - Expected steady-state: 80 qps; peak (w/ batching & autoscale): ~300–350 qps
  - Commit options: 12mo (12% off list), 24mo (20% off), 36mo (26% off + 5% onboarding credit)
  - Use-case fit: long-context, KV-heavy inference and large-batch scoring

2) Balanced (predictable latency + good memory)
  - Pool: 12x A100-80GB
  - Expected steady-state: 80 qps; peak: ~250 qps
  - Commit options: same tiered discounts as above
  - Use-case fit: steady QPS, mid-size KV caches, teams that want tried-and-true ops

3) Cost-optimized (short prompt, high concurrency)
  - Pool: 16x L40S-48GB
  - Expected steady-state: 80 qps; peak: ~220 qps (higher concurrency per node)
  - Commit options: same tiered discounts; note lower hardware list price
  - Use-case fit: stateless, small-context inference where perf/$ is priority

Other commercial details - Throughput guarantees: we offer SLA-backed uptime + latency SLOs; if committed SLOs are missed we provide pro-rated pool-month credits (language in attached SLA).
- Fallback policy: automatic reroute to alternative pool (A100 fallback with small surcharge) if reserved GPUs are temporarily unavailable.
- Procurement steps / MAP (proposal):
  * Week 0: Sign NDA / finalize commercial terms (PO or MSA signature)
  * Week 1–2: Pilot provisioning (sandbox pool + smoke tests)
  * Week 3–6: Production rollout and traffic ramp (metering & traceroutes)
  * Month 1 invoice and enablement review

If you can tell us which option you prefer (Throughput / Balanced / Cost-opt), we’ll send a short IO/PO-ready quote and run a quick capacity check for your desired region. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the numbers.

Best,
